KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): when a switch/if tree ends in ONE shared call but the only remaining diff is a register swap between a parameter copied for that call (e.g. `move t1,a1` saved for a stack arg) and a branch-local temp, the original probably had the call duplicated in several leaf paths (`... f(arg0,x,y,&cb,arg1,0,0); return; }` in one branch, plus the call after the switch). Jump2 cross-jumping merges the identical tails after register allocation, so the instruction count is the same, but the extra uses of the parameter raise its global-alloc priority and the registers swap into place.

The row arithmetic then takes a0 and the parameter moves to a2, which closed a 155-point regalloc gap. KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): when several switch arms each end in a `do {...} while (i < N)` loop over a u8 i and then fall into one shared tail indexed by i, check the target's tail. If it has no `andi sX,0xff` of its own (it reuses the loop test's `andi v1,s3,0xff`, so reorg puts the tail's first insn, e.g. `sll s0,v1,1`, in each arm's `j` delay slot), assign the masked index to ONE shared u32 local in every loop condition, `} while ((n = i) < N);`, and index the tail with n. Use u32, not s32: s32 gives slti instead of sltiu. A plain `goto`/`break` to the tail recomputes the andi.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): the block `bgez rS, 1f; move rD, rS; negu rD, rD; 1:` is MIPS's abssi2 pattern and comes from `__builtin_abs(x)` (or abs(x)). Writing `(x<0)?-x:x` or `d=x; if(x<0) d=-x;` gives `bltzl`+`negu` and different scheduling instead. Also: `or a,b; nor; or; ori 0x10` order follows C left-assoc, e.g. `s = s | ~f | 16;` vs `s |= ~f | 16` (latter emits ori before or).

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): for a read-modify-write through a computed address (`lhu; sll; addu v0,v0,sB; addu v0,v0,sO; lw a0,(v0); ...; sw v1,(v0)`), write the compound assignment on the address expression itself, `*(u32*)(idx*4 + base + off) /= 100;`. Keeping a pointer local (`p = ...; *p /= 100;`) adds a pseudo and swaps registers or addu operands. Also, when a later block reuses a function-wide temp (v, idx) and the target there uses $at addressing and low v-regs, declare fresh block-scoped locals for that block.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): if the target adds a sum of products into a register that is separate from the consumer's input/output (`mul.s f10,..; mul.s f2,..; mul.s f0,..; add.s f10,f10,f2; add.s f10,f10,f0; <op> f0,f10`), give the sum its own variable and add each term in its own statement: `s = a*a; s += b*b; s += c*c; r = op(s);`. A single expression ties the registers differently. Also: a tail of `li v0,..; bc1t L; ...; lbu v0,G; L: andi v0,v0,0xff` (andi at the join, copied into a delay slot) comes from a signed-char local returned as u8 (`s8 r`). s32/u8/s16 locals let gcc drop the andi.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): if the target copies a pointer at a branch join (`L: move v1,a3`), then uses the copy for a few loads and goes back to the original register later, the copy is a pointer local assigned on BOTH arms of the preceding if: `if (c) { f |= X; p = e; } else p = e;` then use p. gcc 2.7 has no global CSE, so a pseudo with two sets survives past the join. A single `p = e;` (at the top or in a block) gets folded away by cse.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): if the target RE-LOADS and re-tests a value just tested by the enclosing if (e.g. `lb v1,(a0); bne v1,13,..; lb v0,(a0); beq v0,13,..`), but your version lets CSE fold the second test away, the re-tested code is the top of a DO-WHILE loop: its top label has two predecessors, so CSE can't use the outer test. The do-while's back-edge condition then gets jump-threaded past the re-test, which shows up as a `beql v0,K,L; addiu p,p,1` into the middle of the loop. Example: `do { while (*p++ != '\r') { if (!(p<end)) break; } if (p == end) break; p++; } while (*p == '\r');`.

V-Rally: loads from 0x800D0634..0x800D0644 in the target have a raw `lw rX,0x634(rX)` (no %lo reloc). Reading them through a constant-address cast, `#define RAWD ((T **)0x800D0634)` then `RAWD[n]`, leaves only the lui operand row different, where the symbol D_800D0634 leaves both lui and lw different. The cast changes alias analysis, though: a raw-address load may get scheduled above stores through other global pointers. Keep the `extern T *D_800D0634[5]` array form wherever that reordering appears, and use the cast elsewhere.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): if the target keeps float locals on the stack and reloads them at every use across a call (`swc1 f0,0x38(sp)` ... `lwc1 f4,0x38(sp)` repeatedly) and one of those stores sits in a jal delay slot, the locals are a plain (non-volatile) array such as `f32 v[3];`, not volatile scalars. gcc never moves volatile memory refs into delay slots, so volatile scalars leave `swc1; jal; nop`. The array also keeps a never-read element store (e.g. v[1]) that a scalar would lose.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): in a goto-built endless loop (`loop: ...; goto loop;`, so no loop notes), an FP temp pair can come out swapped (e.g. target `lwc1 f2,G; mtc1 K->f0; mul.s f2,f2,f0; trunc.w.s f0,f2`, yours f0/f2 the other way round). Wrap just that one statement in `do { ... } while (0);`. The loop notes change local-alloc's register choice without letting loop.c hoist anything. Turning the whole goto into `for(;;)` also fixes the FP regs, but it lets loop.c hoist constants (an extra sdc1 f20 and a bigger frame).

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): when the target spills pointer locals across calls (`sw tX,0x14(sp)` ... `lw tX,0x14(sp)`) and your spill slots hold the same values in a different order, reorder the local DECLARATIONS. Pseudos are numbered in declaration order and reload hands out spill slots in pseudo order (lowest number gets the lowest offset). Local arrays (e.g. a `pad[2]` filler) are placed BELOW all spill slots, so a filler array moves every slot up by its size. It cannot stand in for frame space the target has above the spills.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): if the target has one block that two else-if tests branch into (one jumps to the block, the other falls into it) AND that block reuses a constant already sitting in a register (e.g. `sh a2,0x20(a0)` where a2=1 was set earlier), write two separate identical bodies, not a goto label. Cross-jumping merges the duplicates after CSE has substituted the register into each copy. A goto/shared label has two predecessors, so CSE loses the value and emits a fresh `li`.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): if a range check on a u8 global needs a SIGNED compare with no zero-extend (`lbu v1,G; slti v0,v1,3; beqz ..; bnez v1,..`), write `if ((s16) G >= 3)` directly on the global. An s32 temp (`t = G; if (t >= 3)`) adds `andi a1,v1,0xff` and moves the later uses to a1. A bare `G >= 3` or `(s32)G > 2` becomes a different compare and is much worse.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): if a loop's second counter is initialised (e.g. `addiu sK,zero,1`) AFTER the loop-invariant values hoisted ahead of the loop (e.g. `addiu s7,s1,0x4c`), while yours puts it before them, the counter is not a C variable. KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): this applies to F3DEX-style triangle/quad words with vertex indices, e.g. `w0 = (n<<17)|((n+1)<<9)|((n+2)*2)|0x07000000; w1 = (n<<17)|(((n+2)*2)<<8)|((n+3)*2)`. Suppose the target computes `addiu aX,n,2; sll aX,aX,1` once and reuses it later via `sll aX,aX,8`, but yours folds the expression to `(n+2)<<9` or `n*2+4`. That is the GBI _SHIFTL(v*2,...,8) mask. gcc drops the andi when n is known small, but the cast still blocks the fold.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 (V-Rally): when the target keeps a redundant while-loop entry test after an `if (same cond) { while (cond) ... } else return x;` guard (the test is re-done on one path), but your compile drops it, re-read the tested variable at the top of the if body (`c = *p;` again, even though c already holds *p). Hand-written assembly: the disassembly marks both loop bodies "handwritten instruction".
